composition.serve_who: This is a BUILDING/STRUCTURAL GA, not a schematic GA: the title is “Steering System GA,” and the perspective, plan, sections, dimensions, mounting details, mirrored port/starboard geometry, toe-in/Ackermann tables, and structural callouts define the stern installation of the twin-rudder steering system. The central track/car, rod links, steering ropes and lower sheave boxes serve the overall steering system; blade/stock geometry serves the mirrored rudder blades; the specifically labelled autopilot ram and its support serve the autopilot system. No hydraulic, electrical, or other schematic connectivity is shown.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Primary served equipment: the sheet title is “Steering System GA,” and most views locate and dimension the mechanical steering arrangement across the stern, including the central car/track, rod links, rope/sheave runs, steering cylinders/arms, and port/starboard symmetry.

functions.label: Mechanically command both rudders
functions.what_it_does: Transfers helm or pilot steering movement through the stern-mounted steering mechanism to turn the port and starboard rudders with the designed Ackermann relationship; the port and starboard arrangements are mirrored about vessel centerline.
key_components: central movable steering car and track
steering rope runs serving the wheel inputs
port and starboard lower sheave boxes
steering cylinders/actuators shown at each rudder stock
functions.dry_data: Building/structural GA; twin-rudder stern installation; neutral toe-in 1.8° with 2044 mm rod links; toe-in adjustment table spans 2025–2056 mm rod length for 0–3°; car travel/race ±365 mm from CL; Ackermann table: car position 0/98/212/316.5/364.3 mm corresponds to inside rudder 1.8/10/20/30/35° and outside rudder −1.8/6.3/16.0/25.3/30.0°.
functions.sheet_region: Whole sheet, especially upper-left perspective, upper-right plan, lower-right transverse arrangement, and system/Ackermann notes.

functions.label: Provide steering-path redundancy
functions.what_it_does: Provides three independent steering inputs—two wheel paths plus pilot—so stated single-path failures do not remove all rudder control.
key_components: independent port and starboard rod/link arrangements
functions.dry_data: Safety basis stated on sheet: no separate emergency steering system required; one rod failure leaves one rudder active; one wheel failure leaves the second wheel controlling both rudders; failure of both wheels leaves the pilot controlling the rudders.
functions.sheet_region: Bottom-center SAFETY NOTES, supported by the mirrored arrangement in the perspective and plan views.

functions.label: Locate and accommodate steering mechanism
functions.what_it_does: Defines the physical envelope, clearances, penetrations, and local support arrangement required for steering mechanism movement and installation at the stern.
key_components: central track support with 16 mm tapping-plate insert
tri-beam penetration for pilot rod movement
functions.dry_data: Track support references DWG 108-01-150-004; sheave boxes are to be bonded horizontally; dimensions are in millimetres unless otherwise indicated.
functions.sheet_region: Lower-center Section B-B and Detail E, upper-center Detail A, upper-right port lower sheave-box detail, and lower-right transverse view.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The transverse arrangement and Section C-C explicitly show the port and starboard rudder stocks/blades, their bearing locations, neutral toe-in geometry, and linkage attachment. This builds on the established mirrored-blade identity rather than treating each side as unrelated equipment.

functions.label: Generate directional control
functions.what_it_does: The mirrored port and starboard blades rotate about their stocks to create the vessel’s commanded steering response, with designed neutral toe-in and differential inside/outside angles.
functions.dry_data: Twin mirrored rudders; neutral toe-in 1.8° at 2044 mm rod-link length; Section C-C through rudder blade is shown rotated 26°; installation spans the hull shell and the stated upper/lower bearing structures.
functions.sheet_region: Lower-left Section C-C and Detail D, lower-right transverse arrangement and toe-in/Ackermann notes, upper-left perspective.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: A dedicated section labels the autopilot ram support, its bulkhead attachment, and the penetration needed for pilot-rod movement; the safety notes identify the pilot as the third independent steering path.

functions.label: Actuate steering through the pilot path
functions.what_it_does: Moves the steering mechanism through the dedicated autopilot ram/rod arrangement so the pilot can remain in control if both wheel steering paths fail.
key_components: ram support bolted through bulkhead L
functions.dry_data: Mechanical installation only; ram support is bolted through BHD L; tapping plates are bonded on the forward face; tri-beam penetration is sized to suit pilot-rod movement. Actuator make, stroke, force, and control details are not given on this GA.
functions.sheet_region: Lower-center Section B-B and adjacent note; bottom-center SAFETY NOTES.

facts: The steering installation interfaces with the hull shell, deck inner skin, hull outer skin, TRI-BEAM 11, PARTITION LM1, PARTITION LM2, and bulkhead L.
Upper bearing structure is referenced to DWG 108-05-151-001; lower bearing structure is referenced to DWG 108-05-151-002.
A penetration is required in the tri-beam to suit pilot-rod movement.
The autopilot ram support is bolted through bulkhead L with tapping plates bonded on the forward face.
The central track support uses a 16 mm tapping-plate insert and references DWG 108-01-150-004.
Design waterline, datum 0, hull inner/outer skins, and stern framing are shown as installation references rather than steering connectivity.

discarded_as_clutter: Bill-of-materials item-number balloons and repeated BOM rows; component functions and positions are retained without duplicating procurement metadata.
Repeated port/starboard callouts where the sheet establishes a mirrored arrangement.

View titles, scales, centerline/DWL repeats, section letters, detail bubbles, projection note, general tolerances, edge-breaking note, approval/review signatures, dates, revision history, sheet format, and title-block administration.
Drawing-number repeats except structural reference drawings needed to locate installation interfaces.
Decorative/rendered hull geometry not carrying a dimension, equipment callout, or installation fact.
uncertainties: The GA depicts two wheel steering paths as mechanical rope/cable runs, but the wheel stations and complete off-sheet routing are not shown; their remote endpoints and rope lengths cannot be established from this sheet.
The drawing does not provide actuator make/model, ram stroke/force, rope specification, or bearing ratings; these must not be inferred from the GA.
Some small BOM manufacturer/part-number text is not cleanly legible; the identified component roles are sufficient, and part numbers should be captured at inspection only if ever needed.
